llm.summary: This is a documentation-only skill for configuring Gladia audio intelligence features, with privacy considerations users should manage before sending sensitive audio or transcripts.

dimensions.detail: External processing of audio/transcripts is expected for this purpose, but the artifact gives limited privacy, consent, retention, and regulated-data guidance around live audio, PII redaction, and audio-to-LLM usage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown documentation only; no executable files, dependency installation hooks, postinstall steps, or remote payload execution were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to configuration guidance and code examples, prefer the official SDK, and do not contain session hijacking, hidden role changes, destructive commands, or unrelated agent behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, background services, or credential-store access were found. The documentation notes custom metadata may be stored with provider jobs, so users should avoid placing sensitive identifiers there unless appropriate.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose and capabilities are coherent: it documents Gladia transcription intelligence features such as translation, NER, PII redaction, summarization, and audio-to-LLM. These features inherently process audio/transcripts through Gladia or related model processing, which can involve sensitive spoken content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before using this skill on real recordings, confirm that sending audio, transcripts, metadata, and audio-to-LLM prompts to Gladia or downstream model processing is allowed by your policy and by participant consent. Minimize submitted data, enable PII redaction when appropriate, and avoid sensitive metadata or regulated content unless retention and compliance requirements are clear.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The privacy-warning concern is supported in part: the skill explains how to enable sensitive audio intelligence features without much consent or data-governance guidance. This is purpose-aligned documentation for an external audio service, not hidden or deceptive behavior, so it warrants user guidance rather than Review classification.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 results, which is consistent with inspection of a Markdown-only artifact and no executable install or runtime mechanism.
